anchor_comparisons.comparison: The approved L1 task is a discrete projected voxel-pile extraction problem with a small pile, a few targets/hazards, rotation controls, and ray-based mining. Pocket Locksmith d4 instead has three coupled torsions, three contacts, five obstacles, collision checks, and direct handle/camera manipulation. Its continuous articulated geometry, precision, and hidden-handle search place it materially above this L1 reference, though no empirical calibration was available.

anchor_comparisons.comparison: Approved L4 Blind Dice d4 creates a five-gate warehouse route with sparse scanners and hidden rolling orientation; its grader requires a valid sequence through the gates. Pocket Locksmith d4 has fewer discrete route stages but three coupled joints, three contacts, obstacle/atom collision checks, and viewpoint-dependent handle manipulation. Both are plausible L4-scale visual control tasks, trading hidden orientation memory for geometric precision and camera search.

anchor_comparisons.comparison: Approved L5 searches among state-changing swaps: accepted moves cascade, refill the board, change future state, and affect exact score and wave quotas. Pocket Locksmith d5 adds a fourth joint/contact, seven obstacles, smaller steps, and tighter spatial margins, but its kinematic world lacks that changing-board route and exact-score dependency. Pocket d5 is high-end for this mechanic but does not establish equivalence to the L5 anchor.

visible_baseline_solution: In current d4/full, a screenshot-only agent must read the task and canvas: a translucent pocket contains connected atoms/bonds, contact rings and labels mark fit regions, obstacles occupy the volume, and the side console shows viewport/readout plus Certify and Abandon. It must orbit by dragging, inspect projected clearances and visible handles, drag one visible handle at a time, and alternate camera inspection with the three joint adjustments because upstream changes move downstream atoms. It must avoid obstacle/atom clashes and bounds, then certify when all contacts are hit; the exported grader replays the full-mode drag transcript and geometry. Target torsions are not visible, so the normal visual solution uses marked contacts and collision/readout feedback rather than hidden state.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The uncontrolled task is source-equivalent to explicit d4/full: generator fallback is d4, browser default is full, and grader default is full. D4 is materially above the approved L1 voxel reference, broadly comparable to the approved L4 Blind Dice task, and below the approved L5 changing-board/exact-score planning burden. L4 is plausible but uncalibrated. Revise the profile matrix because torsion_tolerance_deg is not enforced and full/simplified modes differ in task-relevant handle access.

findings.claim: torsion_tolerance_deg is exposed and varied in every profile but is not part of the pass predicate.
findings.causal_explanation: Truth stores target_torsions and torsion_tolerance_deg and the grader computes torsion_errors, but browser and server acceptance require contacts, no clashes, and bounds; they never compare torsion errors to torsion_tolerance_deg or require target_torsions.

evidence.explanation: Truth exports target torsions and torsion tolerance.

findings.recommended_action: Remove torsion_tolerance_deg or enforce an intended target-angle predicate, then recalibrate the ladder.

findings.claim: Full and simplified preserve the same generated world and final geometry checks but do not provide the same torsion-action availability or camera action set.
findings.causal_explanation: Simplified button handlers call adjustBond without checking handle visibility. Full pointer interaction starts torsion only on a visible handle, and the grader rejects a full torsion event when hidden. Full orbit accepts arbitrary pointer displacement while simplified orbit uses one fixed camera step. With occlusion enabled, simplified can turn a joint directly that full must first expose.

evidence.explanation: Simplified buttons directly adjust; full pointerdown selects visible handles and maps drag displacement.
Full replay checks handle visibility and source.
Control metadata documents buttons versus viewport/curved-handle manipulation and hidden handles.

findings.recommended_action: Either align action availability/effects if modes should differ only by input surface, or document the direct-access difference and calibrate modes separately.

findings.claim: Source comments intend a non-solved initial pose and safe target geometry, but the generator does not assert those invariants for every seed.
findings.causal_explanation: Contact selection ranks initial clearance but can fall back to a target site if no ranked candidate exists. The shown generation path checks target point clearance from obstacles but does not assert target nonbonded atom separation or an initial contact miss before export.

evidence.explanation: Contact-site selection ranks initial clearance but includes a target-site fallback without an invariant assertion.
Obstacle placement uses target points and obstacle clearance; the cited path does not validate every target atom-pair separation.

findings.recommended_action: Use parent multi-seed generation/runtime checks to confirm initial non-success and target solvability; add generator assertions if violated.

concise_summary: Pocket Locksmith's uncontrolled task is source-equivalent to d4/full and d4 is a plausible, though uncalibrated, L4 placement: screenshot-only articulated-pose fitting uses three coupled joints, contacts, collisions, bounds, occlusion, and direct manipulation. The d1-d5 ladder is source-distinguished by active geometry and precision, and d4 is above the approved L1 anchor and broadly comparable to approved L4 while below the approved L5 changing-board reference. Revise the matrix because torsion_tolerance_deg is not enforced and full/simplified modes differ in hidden-handle access and camera action granularity.
limitations: No browser, runtime, multi-seed, human, or computer-use-agent checks were performed; parent performs runtime checks separately.
No previous audits, reviews, or historical pre-control implementation were read.
The solver reads private truth and demonstrates wiring only, not the normal screenshot-only burden.
Absolute L1-L5 labels remain provisional without calibration measurements.
